messages.author: c8fe4075ec631c03
messages.subject: rest adaptors
parts:
This is somewhat off-topic, but.

I'm trying to write a web-app using shiny against a RESTful API.

The API has an impedance mismatch with my application in a number of ways:

  * some operations are dog slow
  * it fails to supply correct mime types
  * some files require extensive reprocessing in R, which R isn't great at speed-wise

Caching of raw and transformed results could definitely help with this, so I'm considering building a whole new RESTful API which proxies on to the original API, but provides the interface I actually want, plus caching, plus on the wire transcoding.

I have asked stack overflow how to solve this, http://stackoverflow.com/questions/17453989/adapter-proxy-for-restful-apis/17455070#17455070, but the attempt is almost certainly doomed, since such questions inevitably turn into a vi-vs-emacs fest, and moderators (of which I am one) tend to kill them off early.

However, having looked at clojure ring, and squid, which fail to please in various ways, I discovered that node.js http-proxy (https://github.com/nodejitsu/node-http-proxy) pretty much meets my needs.  It's a mature proxy that allows for the introduction of middleware on specific routes, and while I haven't discovered whether it can do stream processing, my guess it that it won't be too hard.

I could simply put the caching into my application, but that would complify the application, force R's serial processing on to a parallel problem, and not be re-usable for other clients.  I also hope that by allowing me and others to build a new, nicer API with demonstrable improvements as an adaptor on the original one will spur improvements in the base API!  It's also easier to test this way.

I'm letting you guys know because I am getting an elegant vibe out of this way of working.

-Alex
